title: Review of the interim negative CIPS gene-selection finding on fresh seed 7: again no birth advantage for +50% catalysis (g2 0.049 vs g1 0.056 births per body per 1000 t; twin 0.073 vs 0.060), the population holds at 11-16 bodies by division under washout, and the higher g2 share with the trait (0.49 vs 0.15) follows swap hits, not births
summary: sel.py and world.py copied unchanged, seed 7, a2 0.5 and the a2 0 twin with the same swap and washout streams (swap_T 200, wash_T 1000 from t=6000), T=20000 (the finding ran 30000). ana.py: g2 share over t=15000-20000 0.49 (trait) vs 0.15 (twin), ending 8/15 vs 1/12; the trait arm's rises at t=15100-17300 coincide with three swap hits that the twin's draws do not land on bodies (twin hits at 19500 and 19900). rates.py from t=6000: births g1/g2 7/3 (trait) and 9/2 (twin), per-capita 0.056/0.049 and 0.060/0.073 per 1000 t. Bodies from t=6000: mean 13.4 (11-16) and 12.7 (11-14) with 14 removals each. labkit re-run of the a2 0.5 world on seed 7 (192^2, T=12000): 7 persistent splits, generation 2, 0 merges, s rim membrane-like on the top tracks.

observations.H: rates_s7.txt: per-capita births of g2 0.049 vs g1 0.056 with the trait, 0.073 vs 0.060 in the twin: no birth advantage for +50% catalysis; ana_s7.png: share differences follow swap hits; population 11-16 bodies under 14 removals

seeds_run.result: negative for selection reproduced; steady washed population reproduced

controls_run.H: a2 0 twin with the same swap and washout streams (sel_s7_a0.0.json)

verdicts.limitation: One seed, T=20000 rather than 30000, and only 10-11 births per arm after t=6000, so per-capita rates are noisy. I ran the interim world as published, with the partial-swap artifact the finding names (a swap on a body crossing the box edge); I did not check whether any of my seed's 6-7 swap hits were partial. 'Supported' here means the negative result replicates.
